subject: Novum Health — execution locations, subprocessors, and deletion timeline
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@novumhealth.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: security@novumhealth.ai
Subject: Question: where do Novum requests run & deletion guarantees

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking time earlier this week. We're working through our procurement security checklist and need a concise mapping of where LLM inference requests and any derived artifacts are processed for Redwood's hosted offering. Specifically: 

- Which cloud regions do requests touch (ingress, inference, KV cache, ephemeral storage)?
- Which subprocessors (cloud, logging, monitoring, analytics) might see request metadata or logs?
- Do any requests cross borders (EU↔US, APAC↔US) for typical production usage?
- What is the guaranteed deletion timeline for prompt payloads and cached prefixes, and how is deletion demonstrated (audit logs, deletion certificates)?

We're trying to lock a mutual action plan this week so a short, technical-answer email with any supporting attachments or links would be ideal. If you prefer a quick 20-min call, let me know availability.

Best,
Claire
Claire Huang
Head of Security & Privacy
Novum Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@novumhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Question: where do Novum requests run & deletion guarantees

Claire —

Appreciate the clear list. High level answers below; looping in Marissa (security) and Karthik (privacy) for the subprocessor inventory and evidence artifacts. Attaching a short processing-path diagram and our current subprocessor CSV for your procurement packet.

- Regions: In hosted mode, requests are routed to the nearest active inference region by policy. We currently operate inference endpoints in us-central1 (Iowa), us-west2 (Oregon), eu-west1 (Belgium), and asia-southeast1 (Singapore). Ingress terminates at the edge region (API gateway) closest to the client; model execution and KV cache allocation occur in the assigned inference region. Ephemeral caches are local to the serving instance and not persisted beyond the instance lifetime.

- Subprocessors: Primary cloud provider services (compute, object storage for artifacts, KMS), monitoring/observability (our telemetry pipeline), and a limited analytics partner for aggregated usage insights may see metadata. See attached CSV for full list and contract status.

- Cross-border transfers: By default we route requests to the region closest to the caller. If you require strict EU-only processing, we can enforce region pinning at the account level (hosted) or recommend Dedicated/Private deployments. For standard hosted usage, some control-plane metadata (account identifiers, billing records) is stored in our control plane located in the US and may be replicated for availability; inference payloads are executed in the region selected and are not routinely replicated cross-region unless explicitly configured.

- Deletion guarantees: Prompt payloads and derived ephemeral caches are retained for up to 30 days by default for debugging and quality monitoring; customers can request shorter retention or immediate deletion. Deletions are recorded in our audit logs; we can provide time-stamped deletion events and an on-demand deletion runbook. For high-assurance needs, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments with customer-managed keys and retention controls.

Marissa / Karthik — can you attach the latest subprocessor inventory and a sample deletion-audit extract we can share with Novum?

Happy to jump on a call if helpful. I have availability Mon 8/17 10–12 PT.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:40:00 -0700
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@novumhealth.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Question: where do Novum requests run & deletion guarantees

Claire —

Following up with technical specifics and the artifacts Sean promised. Attached: redwood_subprocessor_inventory_v1.csv (column: service, vendor, data-scope, contract-status) and a short retention/deletion playbook (retention-deletion-playbook.docx). A few clarifications below: 

- Execution path: Request flow = API gateway (edge) -> regional routing service -> inference cluster (gpu pool) -> KV cache local to cluster. Persistent artifacts: model binaries (read-only), checkpoint snapshots for model upgrades (stored in object storage), and customer-configurable logs (optional).

- Exact subprocessors that may access request metadata: cloud compute/storage provider (for ephemeral disks / model artifacts), managed KMS provider (for encryption key storage; we also support customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private), telemetry backend (metrics/traces), and our analytics partner (aggregated, pseudonymized usage metrics only). The CSV details which subprocessors have access to request payloads vs. metadata.

- Cross-border behavior: For hosted accounts without region pinning, routing is latency-first; in practice most EU-origin traffic stays in EU regions, but fallback to US regions can occur when capacity/availability dictates. We provide a processing map on request and can set hard-region constraints per account (policy enforcement).

- Deletion evidence: We produce an audit event for each deletion request (event includes object-id, deletion-type, requestor, and timestamp). We can export a time-bounded deletion manifest (CSV) showing object IDs and deletion timestamps for your SOC/investigation needs. For Novum, we could schedule a weekly export during procurement review.

Attachments: processing-path-diagram.pdf (a single-page flow), redwood_subprocessor_inventory_v1.csv, retention-deletion-playbook.docx.

If you want a signed attestation or a sample audit extract (anonymized), reply and we will generate one.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Principal Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@novumhealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Question: where do Novum requests run & deletion guarantees

Sean / Marissa —

Thank you for the fast turnaround and the artifacts. The CSV and playbook look good; we'd like the following to close the security questions for procurement: 

1) A time-bounded deletion manifest for test data (anonymized) showing deletion timestamps — a one-off extract will suffice.
2) Confirmation that EU pinning can be enabled at account level for hosted (we may still evaluate Dedicated).
3) A contact for escalation during onboarding (if we detect cross-border flows we didn't expect).

Can you confirm 1–2 today? If yes we'll route to legal and pull procurement.

Best,
Claire
